title: Proposition 1: Authorizes Bonds for Housing Affordability Programs. Legislative Statute.

context.text: Placed on the ballot by the Legislature as SB 417 (Chapter 16, Statutes of 2026). Final legislative votes: Senate 29 ayes, 2 noes; Assembly 61 ayes, 7 noes.

question.text: AUTHORIZES BONDS FOR HOUSING AFFORDABILITY PROGRAMS. LEGISLATIVE STATUTE. Authorizes $11.25 billion in state general obligation bonds for housing affordability programs, including for California veterans, and to finance housing development projects seeking federal tax credits. Allocates funds: $5.1 billion to build and rehabilitate multifamily rental housing; $2.1 billion to acquire, rehabilitate, or preserve affordable housing units, and provide supportive housing for those experiencing homelessness; $1.25 billion for state-funded mortgages for California veterans; $1.1 billion for homeownership and downpayment assistance; $1 billion for farmworker, tribal, and student housing; $500 million for housing infrastructure; and $200 million to support local housing programs.

summary.text: Allows the state to sell $11.25 billion in general obligation bonds: a $10 billion bond for state housing programs repaid from the General Fund and a $1.25 billion bond for veterans home loans repaid by veterans' loan payments. Per the Legislative Analyst, funds go to affordable multifamily housing ($7.2 billion), homeownership programs ($1.1 billion), infrastructure ($500 million), farmworker housing ($450 million), student housing ($350 million), tribal housing ($200 million) and local pilot programs ($200 million). Fiscal impact: increased state General Fund cost of $500 million to $600 million annually for about 25 years; the veterans program has operated at no direct state cost.

measure.yesMeans: The state could borrow $11.25 billion to support veterans and affordable housing.
measure.noMeans: The state could not borrow $11.25 billion to support veterans and affordable housing.

argumentsFor.text: Official argument in favor, signed by Anni Chung (Self-Help for the Elderly), Jeffery Freitas (California Federation of Teachers) and John H. Ing (US Vets): "Prop. 1 doesn’t raise taxes and every dollar comes with strict accountability and public reporting." It also says: "Prop. 1 builds more homes working people can actually afford."
Also in the official argument: "Dedicates $1.25 billion solely to veterans' housing and homeownership opportunities through the existing CalVet Home Loan Program."
